entities.summary: Andreas Stöberl, better known by his Latinised name Andreas Stiborius (Boius), was a German humanist astronomer, mathematician, and theologian working mainly at the University of Vienna from 1495 to 1515. He was a key figure in the Vienna School of Astronomical Theology, which attempted to reconcile Aristotelian philosophy with Ptolemaic astronomy. Stöberl's most notable work was the Astronomical Theology, a treatise on the relationship between astronomy and theology that was widely read and influential in its time. The work of Andreas Stöberl reflects the cultural and intellectual currents of late medieval Europe, where humanism, astrology, and theological inquiry converged. His legacy can be seen in the development of astronomical and mathematical education at European universities, particularly in the Austrian and German-speaking regions. The Vienna School of Astronomical Theology, of which Stöberl was a part, played a significant role in shaping the intellectual landscape of 16th-century Europe. As a result, Stöberl's contributions are best understood within the broader context of the European Renaissance and the early modern period's emphasis on humanism and intellectual inquiry.
